chapter: Hutto 1978-79: NBC, radio and the N'goma drums
title: Larry Clinton, RCA and NBC
summary: Morehouse explains NBC took on Larry Clinton because his records sold, tying RCA and NBC together.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: 'Love's Old Sweet Song', we brought those. We'll play those for you, 'Twelfth Street Rag.' And the 'Royal Garden Blues' which is really the 'Memphis Blues'. Okay, we'll play those for you. When Larry Clinton started his band, I guess it was just a recording band at first and apparently you were on the second recording session he had.
Well Larry Clinton came into the NBC because his records were selling. And NBC wanted a guy whose records Could sell. So that's why they got him.
To sort of tie in with RCA and NBC.
So you were on both sides of that.
There were only a couple of big record makers, Columbia, RCA.
